newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Australian named head of UN Iraq disarmament group.
newsitem.headline: Australian named head of UN Iraq disarmament group.

text.p: Australia's U.N. ambassador, Richard Butler, was named on Thursday as executive chairman of the U.N. commission in charge of Iraqi disarmament, the United Nations announced.
He replaces Rolf Ekeus of Sweden, who has led the U.N. Special Commission, known as UNSCOM, since its inception in 1991. Ekeus expects to leave in July to become Sweden's ambassador in Washington.
The announcement was made by U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard on behalf of Secretary-General Kofi Annan. U.S. and Australian officials welcomed the appointment.

UNSCOM is in charge of eliminating Iraq's weapons of mass destruction. The oil embargo and other sanctions against Iraq, imposed after it invaded Kuwait in 1990, cannot be lifted until the commission is satisfied it has accounted for all its biological, chemical and ballistic arms.

Butler, 54, known as articulate and blunt, has been involved in disarmament affairs since 1983, when he was appointed Australia's first ambassador at the Geneva-based Conference on Disarmament for five years.
He was instrumental last year in saving the nuclear test ban treaty by getting the General Assembly to open it for signature after India blocked it in negotiations in Geneva.
